grand_strategy.reading:
Bulgaria's strategy is that of a small, poor, shrinking member of two clubs
that has just chosen a leader who sells distance from both while keeping the
benefits of each. The euro (1 Jan 2026), full Schengen (1 Jan 2025), the NATO
battlegroup, the F-16s and the Westinghouse fuel are the anchor and nobody in
power is seriously proposing to cut it; what moves is the margin. Rumen Radev,
elected on 19 April 2026 with a single-party majority, uses the one thing a
small state has inside the EU, the veto, on Patriarch Kirill, on Lukoil's
founder and on North Macedonia, and pays for it by leaving Ukraine's
coalition and freezing state arms aid, while the factories keep selling.
The Luttwakian pattern is plain: each gain in leverage (the veto, the special
manager at Burgas, the transit corridor, the defence industry) is bought
with a loss in trust among the same partners who guarantee the anchor, and
the paradox of the North Macedonia block shows the end of that road.
Signals that are not rows: Zakharova said on 29 May 2026 that Sofia showed
no sign of restoring dialogue with Moscow and on 14 Jul that it was 'too weak'
to help Ukraine, not turning toward Russia; the pivot is therefore toward
caution, not toward the Kremlin. The oligarch network of Peevski, Magnitsky-listed
by the US in June 2021, lost its place in government in April 2026, but the
underlying fragility (eight elections in five years, a cabinet toppled by a
budget in December 2025) has not yet been tested by a hard budget under Radev.
What to watch: the Lukoil licences (reported to run to the end of October 2026),
the 21st-package endgame, whether Skopje and Sofia talk again before the
Council's next enlargement report, and whether the 15-month BOTAS suspension
ends with a renegotiated or a litigated contract.

stances.note: No source calls the relationship 'rival'; the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Bulgaria is a NATO and EU member that expelled Russian diplomats in 2020-22, put Lukoil's Bulgarian subsidiaries under a state special manager under US sanctions (Nov 2025), is moving Kozloduy off Russian fuel and carries Russian gas only as a transit state; Zakharova said on 29 May 2026 that Sofia showed 'no sign' of restoring dialogue. stances_toward.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Bulgaria is the first obstacle on Skopje's EU path: it has blocked the opening of negotiations since 2020 and, with the 2022 French proposal, requires the constitution to name Bulgarians (Zhelyazkov, Oct 2025: Sofia adds no new condition to the 2022 proposal). Skopje answers with two conditions (rights for Macedonians in Bulgaria; no further bilateral vetoes) and the Commission notes that no steps have been taken. Incidents keep the wound open: the Ivan Mihailov club sentence (Jun 2025), the arson of two Bulgarian embassy cars in Skopje (15 Jun 2026, suspect detained, motive unknown). The grade is rival, not ally, although both are NATO members (the dataset would derive 'ally'): Sofia's claim that Macedonian language and history are Bulgarian is a contest over identity, and the bilateral friendship treaty of 2017 and Corridor 8 are working in parallel. Trend stable: von der Leyen's visit of 2 Oct 2026 produced a first step, but no movement on the constitution. Bond - grievance: history, language, the 1943 Vatasha anniversary a day after the arson.

relations_to.summary: Mickoski says there will be no constitutional amendment adding Bulgarians while he is prime minister unless Bulgaria first guarantees rights for the Macedonian community and the EU guarantees no further bilateral vetoes; on 28 May 2026 he said the government was ready to 'pay the price' of delayed accession. Sofia says it adds no condition to the 2022 proposal.

relations_to.summary: Skopje's first condition for any amendment is that the Macedonian community in Bulgaria receives the rights guaranteed by international law and human-rights conventions; Mickoski said he was not asking for a change to Bulgaria's constitution. Foreign minister Mucunski in April 2026 asked for 'minimal reciprocity'.

relations_to.summary: Two vehicles with diplomatic plates were set on fire in front of the Bulgarian embassy in Skopje on 15 Jun 2026; a 44-year-old suspect was detained and has admitted the act (Mickoski), motive unknown. Bulgarian President Iotova called it an attack on Bulgaria; Mickoski condemned it.

relations_to.summary: President Siljanovska-Davkova met Bulgarian President Iotova in Sofia on 10 Jun 2026 on the sidelines of the South-East European Cooperation Process summit; she said Sofia's concerns went beyond the amendments to history and the joint history commission, and Mucunski asked for assurances of no further demands.

relations_to.summary: Ljupcho Georgievski, head of the banned Ivan Mihailov Cultural Club in Bitola and a dual citizen, received a one-year suspended sentence (two years' probation) in June 2025 for quoting Mihailov on social media; Bulgaria's foreign minister called it 'categorically unacceptable' and a protest was held outside the Macedonian embassy in Sofia. The 2023 law bans organisations named after figures the state deems controversial.
